assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, both read end to end: CINDERELLA_GIRLS_KANZAKI_RANKO_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (V1, 65,043 bytes, status active_provisional, veto false) and CINDERELLA_GIRLS_KANZAKI_RANKO_MONOGRAPH_AUDIT.md (V1, 40,105 bytes, status canonical, veto false, overall disposition PRESERVE_WITH_TARGETED_REVISIONS). Both rest on one integrated packet of the Cinderella Girls Mobage social game and Starlight Stage: 195 target-confirmed scenes, 2,219 Ranko utterances, Deresute text complete against the released categorized inventory, Mobage structurally incomplete, audio representative only. They locate claims by Deresute story and card ID, by Memorial and by Mobage Refresh Room, not by line. Where they differ, the canonical audit governs. The 2015 television anime and every other adaptation are excluded. The project's corpus map was read for authority and retrieval order only. The character packet and extraction data are outside Git and uncurated, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The whole recovered game corpus as both items read it, from Memorials 1-5 and the early cards through the 2025 episode (DERESTE:STORY:2201481), with located anchors at the 2017 Dark Illuminate crisis and repair (2200431, 5102406), the 2018 events (5103405), the 2019 white-dress card (200730), 2020 card dialogue (200795), the 2021 Chitose Business Commu (7212004), 2022 (201125) and 2024 (2201423). Story Commu chapters and Unlock Starbeat carry no in-story date in the items. Development is treated as overlapping functions under the audit, not as datable stages. Unrecovered Mobage material is outside the boundary.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives five interacting structures (imaginative cognition, protective indirection, authorship inside awkwardness, relational permeability, plural selfhood) and grounds the protective origin in Ranko's own retrospective account (DERESTE:STORY:1000012: the shell 殻 and the dark words that hide weakness). The canonical audit keeps the core (claims 1-3, 5, 8-12 PRESERVE or STRENGTHEN) and replaces the stage sequence with a stack of persistent functions (protective, cognitive, artistic, relational, performative, self-authoring) whose balance changes (audit IV.1). Together they say what changes her response: the kind of exposure she is managing, whether the listener ridicules or tries, whether a task needs clarity, and whether the bond matters (monograph 20, audit IV.3). The account predicts her mistakes: retreat inward, assuming that shared style is understanding, keeping the persona running past fatigue (monograph 19). So B. Not A: the audit's held-out tests are not blind (audit I.3), V1.1 is unwritten, and no high-stakes choice between competing goals is analyzed. Not C: the account discriminates between located situations and was tested on five scenes that were not its argumentative anchors.

The monograph's strata A-H are anchored to dated texts: Memorials 1-5 and early cards, the 2017 Dark Illuminate crisis (2200431, 5102406), the 2019 white-dress card (200730), 2020 card dialogue (200795), the 2021 Chitose Business Commu (7212004), 2022 (201125), 2024 (2201423) and 2025 (2201481). The audit revises this into functional accretion: artistic and relational use is present early, defensive buffering stays available late, and what changes is control, permeability and range (audit claim 4 REVISE, Test 5). It downgrades 2201481 from a final stage to one mature articulation (claim 29). So C. Not B: the audit rejects state boundaries at which a capability is gained or lost, so a dated state is a balance of functions rather than a located state, and the pre-Deresute Mobage development is unrecovered (monograph 23.1). Not D: the dated anchors agree on one direction of change (more register choice and permeability), and the audit locates both its early and late countercases.

This is the strongest layer. The monograph gives five textual modes (full Ranko-go, glossed, porous or mixed, ordinary, alternate authored roles; 4.1-4.5), Japanese forms (我 and 私; 我が友 and 《瞳》持つ者 for Producer; ゆえに, されど, ならば; だもん, えへへ, うん, その), a laughter stance system (ククク, フフフ, ハーッハッハ, えへへ; 15.4) and corpus statistics (465 source-glossed utterances, ellipsis in 1,538 of 2,219 lines; 15.3). The audit verifies the lexicon counts (V.2), rejects one-to-one substitution, and corrects the trigger rule: plain speech follows precision, accommodation, work clarity or naked exposure, and it is not a sincerity meter (claims 13-14, 33; IV.2-IV.3; VIII). So B. Not A: audio is representative only and every acoustic claim is OPEN (claim 36; monograph 15.8), no independent transcript was compared (audit I.1), and context-built metaphor can be checked against the rules but not derived from them. Not C: register choice is conditioned by utterance function and partner, with Japanese anchors and a located countercase for each revision.

Located ordinary conduct includes drawing outfits in her sketchbook and hesitating to show them (DERESTE:CARD:200073), a shopping and music outing with Koume (1000012), answering Chitose plainly that she likes hamburger steak and drawing (7212004), describing herself as quiet at school (201067), the haunted-house outing (1000034, audit Test 1), the umbrella conversation with Asuka (Mobage Refresh Room 46, audit Test 4) and plain speech in rehearsal before she notices the camera (5303004, audit Test 3). The monograph gives a general rule (keep stammers, hunger, fatigue, fear and delight possible; 16.3). So C. Not B: there is no conditioned account of her routines, school life or home, and the audit's 'ordinary domestic ease' trigger is not located (audit IV.2). Mobage normal and seasonal dialogue is unrecovered. Not D: the located scenes recur in a consistent pattern of quiet temperament, art practice and plain preference speech.

Partners are differentiated with stated conditions. Producer (67 shared scenes): an early safe interpreter, then the person who materializes her designs and acts as a secure base, then the person before whom register choice is safest. The audit corrects the early role: he can ask for plain speech for a task without making normalization the price of acceptance (monograph 12; audit claims 6-7, IV.4, VII.1). Asuka (27 scenes): maximal symbolic density with the greatest need for explicit repair (2200431, 5102406; Test 4). Chitose: play inside the frame plus acceptance of ordinary Ranko, kept Chitose-specific (audit claim 22). Koume: presence without full decoding. Nao: permission-giving. Unfamiliar adults: defensive opacity, warmed by sincere effort (5103405). Anastasia: plain speech as accommodation (Story Commu 16, Test 2). So B. Not A: about eight of 109 counterparts are analyzed, and the audit lowers the general outsider 'ethic' to a relational preference (claim 23). Not C: the items say why her register and conduct change with each partner's response to her language, and the audit tests two of these relationships on scenes that were not their anchors.

Her interior is supplied mainly by her own located self-accounts, not by the analyst's inference: the childhood origin and the shell (1000012), the private card episode after the Asuka misunderstanding (2200431: she had not opened her heart and had grown worse at conveying herself to anyone but Producer), no longer fearing herself (200730: 今の私は私自身を怖れない), creating herself (2201423) and the blurred dream and reality (2201481). The monograph reads fear, embarrassment and the wish to be seen without being reduced from these texts, and the audit keeps the reading (claims 1-2 STRENGTHEN). So B. Not A: the source-authored glosses are not inner monologue (monograph 3.1, 23.2; audit claim 11), the late self-accounts are partly downgraded (claim 29), and no interior is given for a high-stakes decision. Not C: the interior states are located in her own words at dated points and explain located behavior.

Two located conflict arcs share one pattern. In the Asuka crisis she is hurt, withdraws, and then speaks plainly to repair the bond (2200431, 5102406). In Unlock Starbeat she hides fatigue under camera observation until group conflict forces disclosure, then apologizes (5303004-5303005). The monograph states the rule 'clarify the person before protecting the aesthetic' (16.5), and the audit keeps it for misunderstanding and repair while denying that seriousness always simplifies her speech (V.4). So C. Not B: the discriminating condition (whether the bond matters) never varies in the located evidence, because both arcs are with valued peers and both end in repair. The response to a mocking stranger is a derived high-confidence prediction (monograph 20), not a located scene, and no conflict with an adversary or an authority is analyzed. Not D: both arcs are located, predict her failure mode, and are confirmed by the audit.

The row claims no ETHICS dimension. Located value-relevant acts are local: her advice to Riina that a borrowed style must be carved into oneself (1000007), telling Nao that a preference of the heart need not shame her (1000012), plain speech so that Anastasia can follow her, followed by an apology (Story Commu 16), and her apologies in the Asuka and Unlock Starbeat arcs. The audit lowers the monograph's 'ethic of imaginative recognition' to a relational preference and states that the packet does not show her applying a general principle across difficult moral conflicts (claim 23 DOWNGRADE, IV.5). So E: these acts answer bounded canon questions only. Not D: no deliberation, weighing or moral choice between alternatives is located.

Play is located mostly as register effect: comic collapse under teasing (Memorial 5: 我が友のいじわるっ ! もうっ !; 3019805), playful imperatives that are not authoritarian (15.2), laughter as a stance system with counts (audit V.3), teasing Nao (13.4), register looseness and food talk with Chitose (7212004, 13.2), the comic fear of the haunted house (1000034) and the cute form of らぶりー♡やみのま (2201423). Conditions are given: low-vulnerability talk sustains maximal theatricality, and Chitose produces looseness. So C. Not B: the items do not say when she starts a joke or game as distinct from being its target, and they give no account of play outside her register. Not D: the stance markers and conditions are located and verified by the audit.

Both items work from one packet: 195 target-confirmed scenes and 2,219 utterances, with Deresute text complete against the released categorized inventory, so absence claims in Deresute are strong. Locators are scene and card IDs (DERESTE:STORY and DERESTE:CARD), not lines. Mobage is structurally incomplete (44 card or profile objects and three Refresh Room scenes), and absence there is not evidence (monograph 23.1; entrypoint rule 5). Audio is representative only (141 containers mapped). The source-conflict document holds no overlapping variant group for Ranko, which means not compared rather than agreement (audit I.1). So B. Not A: the Mobage layer, audio and variant comparison are open. Not C: the Deresute backbone is complete against inventory, and both items state their limits exactly.

Affirmative limits are explicit and located. The audit REJECTs two universal rules (closeness requires total decoding; familiarity lowers Ranko-go density; claims 31-32). It REVISEs the vulnerability-only plain-speech rule with Story Commu 16 (accommodation) and Producer's functional requests for plain speech (Memorial 2, 5103405). It DOWNGRADEs the outsider ethic and the late integration as a final stage (claims 23, 29), and leaves acoustics OPEN (claim 36). The monograph adds prohibitions: she does not believe a literal cosmology, ordinary Ranko is not the only real Ranko, growth does not make her a general extrovert, and 'demon king' is not dominance competence (16.6-16.7, 19.5, 14). So B. Not A: the countertests are not blind, and Mobage absence cannot establish a negative. Not C: each limit cites a located countercase or an explicit disposition.

Many claims are tied to identified scenes, cards and Memorials, and the late texts carry years (2017-2025). But much of the longitudinal prose is unlocated ('later material increasingly'; strata E-F), the Story Commu chapters carry no in-story dates, and the audit treats development as overlapping functions rather than datable stages (claim 4). The Mobage chronology is unrecovered. So C. Not B: a scenario cannot be placed at a located state change except around the Asuka crisis and the dated late texts. Not D: the identified anchors are dense enough to separate early, post-crisis and late material.

conditions: Output is illustrative written Japanese, never quotation; no pitch, tempo, breath or prosody claim is made (audit claim 36).
Register is chosen from the utterance's function (performing, explaining, protecting herself, comforting, affection, repair, work, shared play) under audit VIII, not from emotional intensity alone.
Metaphor is composed from the scene's own objects, using the semantic domains of monograph 3.2-3.3 and audit V.2, never a generic stack of 闇, 魔力, 魂 and 翼.

Plain speech is used for repair, task clarity, accommodation, apology or direct disclosure, and it is never treated as more sincere than Ranko-go; under embarrassment, collapse and stronger buffering are both permitted and neither is predicted.
The partner is Producer, Asuka, Chitose, Koume, Nao, Anastasia or an unfamiliar adult as located; any other idol is a separate, lower-confidence condition limited to the register rules.
Parenthetical glosses are used as semantic bridges only, never as inner monologue, and no trait from the 2015 television anime is admitted.
scenario_readiness.note: The register, function and partner rules, the Japanese forms and the prohibitions constrain illustrative Japanese text closely enough for the declared use. Wording, acoustics and the embarrassment branch stay open.

conditions: Chronology is one named state from cross_scenario_scope. Earlier functions stay available in later states (audit IV.1), and the childhood origin belongs to her at every state.

The situation is one the items sample: a costume or design request, rehearsal or stage fear, an acting or work task that needs clarity, observation that makes the persona compulsory, a peer ashamed of a preference, a fearful setting, a listener who does not understand her language, or a misunderstanding with a valued partner.
The interlocutor is Producer, Asuka, Chitose, Koume, Nao, Anastasia or an unfamiliar adult evaluator; any other idol is a separate, lower-confidence condition without invented history.
When embarrassment is the pressure, comic collapse and intensified buffering are output as alternatives, not predicted.
The response to someone who mocks her language is output as the monograph's derived expectation and labeled unlocated.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named state: early idol life (Memorials 1-5 and the early cards, including 200073), before the 2017 Dark Illuminate crisis; after the Asuka repair (2200431, 5102406); or late, from the 2019 white-dress card (200730) through the 2024 and 2025 episodes (2201423, 2201481). The late default is mature permeability, not an irreversible final synthesis (audit claim 29).
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Producer as secure base and co-creator who may ask for plain speech for a task; Asuka as fluent peer who needs explicit repair; Chitose as playful acceptor; Koume as quiet presence; Nao as a peer ashamed of a preference; Anastasia as a listener she accommodates; an unfamiliar adult as an evaluator who may or may not try to understand. A comparable unsampled idol is a separate, lower-confidence condition, and an unsampled intimate is outside scope.
setting_constraints: Idol work as sampled: lessons, photo shoots, costume design, stage, acting exercise, band camp under observation
Ordinary outings and conversations as sampled: shopping and music, food talk, a haunted house, a weather conversation
No moral dilemma that needs her to weigh competing principles
No resolution of romance terms with Producer

scenario_readiness.note: Supports bounded novel scenes of idol work, ordinary outings and relational repair with sampled partners at one named state. High-stakes moral choice, romance terms and unsampled intimates stay outside scope.

conditions: The setting is an ordinary outing, a meal or food preference, drawing, or a low-pressure conversation like the located Koume, Chitose and Asuka scenes.
She stays socially quiet in group noise (201067), and her preferences (drawing, clothing, music, food) are stated plainly when the partner accepts ordinary Ranko.
No school routine, home life or schedule is invented, and Mobage material that was not recovered is not assumed absent.
scenario_readiness.note: Supports low-stakes ordinary exchanges with sampled peers through located scenes and the quiet-temperament rule, not a model of her routines.

The audit bounds this domain affirmatively: it lowers the monograph's outsider 'ethic' to a relational preference and states that the packet does not show Ranko applying a formulated general principle across difficult moral conflicts (claim 23, IV.5). Her located value acts (Riina, Nao, the Anastasia accommodation, her apologies) show no weighing between alternatives, so a scenario that needs her to deliberate would invent the decisive step.

The monograph bounds this affirmatively. Her closeness to Producer is modeled as secure base and co-creation, and she locates 'home' beside him (200730). The one romance-framed scene is a drama event in which she is asked to formulate an answer to a confession (5109105), and the monograph handles it 'without requiring the artifact to settle franchise-romance ontology'. A romance scenario would have to decide what the item leaves unsettled. Affectionate non-romantic exchanges with Producer are covered under DIALOGUE and CROSS_SCENARIO.

conditions: The task is a sampled idol-work context: lesson, photo shoot, costume design, first or major stage, scripted acting exercise, or band camp under camera observation.
When form obstructs the task she adapts her register and returns to Ranko-go afterwards (5103405; audit claims 25-26); before a stage, fear is acted through a role that permits action (3019804).
Under continuous observation she may keep the persona running and fail to state fatigue until a conflict forces disclosure (5303004-5303005).
No leadership, business negotiation or management role is invented.
scenario_readiness.note: Supports idol-work scenes through located adaptation, fear, design and observation evidence, with her overperformance under surveillance kept as a predicted error.

known_limits.statement: The monograph is V1 and active_provisional. The canonical audit governs its next revision, and that revision is unwritten. Where they differ (stage sequence, Producer and translation, triggers of plain speech, the outsider ethic, the late integration) this record follows the audit.
Under embarrassment she may blurt ordinary speech or hide inside heightened fantasy, and both are canonical (audit VIII.5; claim 33). The items do not say which occurs.
Audio is representative only (141 containers mapped). Pitch, tempo, breathiness, laughter realization and the prosody of register switching are OPEN (monograph 15.8, 23.3; audit claim 36).

The Mobage layer is structurally incomplete, so absence there is not evidence, and the earliest development of Ranko-go, pre-Deresute intimacy with Producer and event-level peer relationships may be revised (monograph 23.1; audit I.1).
The audit's five held-out tests reuse the packet the monograph was built from; they test transfer to scenes that were not its argumentative anchors, not blind prediction (audit I.3).
The packet does not show her applying a general principle across difficult moral conflicts (audit claim 23, IV.5).

The 2025 dream-and-reality episode (2201481) is one late articulation, not proof of an irreversible final synthesis. Withdrawal, embarrassment and buffering remain available late (audit claim 29, IV.6, X).
The monograph declines to settle franchise-romance ontology for the Producer bond (12.3, on 5109105).

Both located conflicts are with valued peers and both end in repair. No conflict with an adversary, an authority or a partner whose bond does not matter is analyzed, and her response to mockery is derived, not located.
The items analyze about eight of 109 indexed interaction counterparts. Behavior with other idols or staff is a transfer, not sampled evidence.

The character packet the entrypoint routes to for source-level checks (chronological scenes, lines, relationship index, audio manifest, gap report) is outside Git and not curated on this subject. No claim here rests on it, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
